interpretations: Each line below is a separate interpretation

Patients are all distinct IDs in Laboratory with at least one row. Each patient's ratio is AVG(HGB)/AVG(HCT), with NULLs ignored independently in each column. The all-patient average is the unweighted mean of those ratios over patients with a computable ratio. Patients with a ratio strictly above it are kept, and PIC averages ignore NULLs
Same as 1, but the kept patients are those with ratio greater than or equal to the all-patient average
Same as 1, but each patient's AVG(HGB) and AVG(HCT) use only rows where both HGB and HCT are non-null
The all-patient average is the pooled ratio, total HGB over total HCT or AVG(HGB)/AVG(HCT) across all Laboratory rows. It is not the mean of per-patient ratios
Patients whose average PIC is NULL (no PIC recorded) are excluded from the comparison group entirely. This also removes them from the all-patient ratio average
Patients whose average PIC is NULL are still part of the all-patient ratio average and can be kept. They are ignored only when averaging the average-PIC values in the summary row
Patients whose average PIC is NULL are kept and their PIC is treated as 0 in the average of average-PIC values
Patients with NULL or zero average HCT (undefined ratio) are excluded from the all-patient average and from the output
"All patients" means every patient in the Patient table, including those with no Laboratory rows, which are excluded because they have no ratio

The "average amount by which ratios exceed the all-patient average" is the mean of (patient ratio − all-patient average) over kept patients. It equals the kept patients' average ratio minus the all-patient average
The "average amount" is a relative excess, the mean of (ratio − overall average) / overall average, as a proportion or percentage
The output is a single row with three columns: average of average PIC, average of ratios, and average excess
The average PIC for each patient is a mean over all of their Laboratory rows (each Date counts equally). It is not a mean of per-date or per-visit values with some other weighting
HGB and HCT averages are computed only over rows with non-null, valid positive values. Zero or placeholder values are treated as missing
Missing interpretations:
Patients with NULL average HGB are excluded from the all-patient average and from the output, because their ratio is undefined
The all-patient average is a weighted mean of per-patient ratios, weighted by each patient's number of Laboratory rows

Each patient's average PIC is computed over only the rows where PIC is non-null, and patients with no PIC are kept in the ratio comparison. This is a variant of the NULL-PIC handling in interpretations 5 and 6, and it fixes the filter used for the HGB and HCT averages
The ratio is computed as the average of per-row HGB/HCT values, not as AVG(HGB)/AVG(HCT)

The "average amount by which ratios exceed the all-patient average" is the mean absolute difference between each kept patient's ratio and the all-patient average. This differs from the signed mean only if kept patients can fall below the average, which is not expected under strict filtering
The summary row also returns a count of kept patients, in addition to the three requested values
If no patient is kept, the summary row returns NULL values or no row
queries:
WITH r AS (
  SELECT ID, AVG(HGB) * 1.0 / NULLIF(AVG(HCT), 0) AS ratio
  FROM Laboratory
  GROUP BY ID
),
k AS (
  SELECT ID
  FROM r
  WHERE ratio IS NOT NULL
    AND ratio > (SELECT AVG(ratio) FROM r WHERE ratio IS NOT NULL)
)
SELECT AVG(PIC)
FROM Laboratory
WHERE ID IN (SELECT ID FROM k);
SELECT ID, AVG(HGB), AVG(HCT)
FROM Laboratory
WHERE HGB IS NOT NULL AND HCT IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY ID;
SELECT AVG(HGB) / AVG(HCT) FROM Laboratory;
SELECT AVG(p.avg_pic * 1.0 / (SELECT AVG(PIC) FROM Laboratory WHERE PIC IS NOT NULL)) AS avg_ratio
FROM (
    SELECT ID, AVG(PIC) AS avg_pic
    FROM Laboratory
    GROUP BY ID
    HAVING AVG(PIC) IS NOT NULL
) AS p;
